1.explanation:
• audits/uses-rel-preconnect-test.js: Contains the unit tests for the preconnect audit logic – how Lighthouse detects missing rel=preconnect hints and computes savings per origin.
• gather/gatherers/link-elements-test.js: Shows how Lighthouse collects <link> elements (including rel=preconnect) from the page’s DOM; critical for verifying preconnect tags are being picked up correctly.
• computed/network-analysis-test.js: Verifies how network records are grouped by origin and classified as “third-party,” which underpins which origins are considered important.
• network-records-to-devtools-log.js: A helper to synthesize DevTools log entries from network records in tests – used by the preconnect audit tests to simulate real traffic data.
• test-utils.js: Provides the harness for running audits in isolation; you’ll need it to assemble trace, network, and link-gatherer artifacts to reproduce the issue programmatically.
1.bug_scenario: In the screenshot from Lighthouse (“Preconnect to required origins”), we see a table of suggested third-party origins (“https://acquisition-1-qa.americanexpress.com”, “https://origin-pqgemapp.americanexpress.com”, etc.) along with their potential savings (e.g. 970 ms). Despite having already added the matching <link rel="preconnect"> tags to the page head, Lighthouse continues listing these URLs under “Consider adding preconnect or dns-prefetch resource hints to establish early connections to important third-party origins.” The UX elements involved are the audit header, the “Learn more” link, and the URL/Potential Savings table. The bug is that Lighthouse isn’t recognizing the existing preconnect hints and keeps recommending them.
